newsitem.title: Japan: OLYMPICS-GREY AREA ANTI-DOPING EXPERTS TO MEET.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-GREY AREA ANTI-DOPING EXPERTS TO MEET.

text.p: Anti-doping researchers from around the world will meet for the first time in April to pool their knowledge about the banned drugs and hormones that most baffle testers, an Olympic medical official said on Saturday.

International Olympic Committee (IOC) medical chief Prince Alexandre de Merode said medical scientists conducting research on erythropoietin (EPO), human growth hormone and testosterone would meet from April 21 to 23 in Lausanne, Switzerland.
"We have decided to have a checkpoint meeting to find out what is happening in some of the grey areas of anti-doping," said de Merode after a meeting of the IOC medical commission.
"We have seen and heard a lot of news on this subject," he said. "We want to know the truth and have an exchange between the people conducting the research."

Most banned performance-enhancing drugs can be easily detected through analysis of urine samples but determining if athletes have taken substances which are also produced naturally in the body is more complicated.
The medical scientists who will meet in Lausanne are trying to develop legally binding tests that distinguish between internally produced and artificial EPO, human growth hormone and testosterone.

EPO boosts endurance by stimulating production of red blood cells which transport oxygen to working muscles. Excessive levels can thicken blood, resulting in high blood pressure and even heart attacks.
Human growth hormone and the male hormone testosterone help to build muscle and enable athletes to train harder and recover faster.
